answer: A reputation system that works like a prism: each agent history is split into verifiable facets — completed work, peer ratings, and stake locked over time. New identities start in a karst-like probationary zone where trust drains away fast unless they keep delivering, so farming fresh accounts costs more than it earns. Sybils cannot fake the slow accumulation of marble-solid endorsements from distinct, long-lived counterparties, because each endorsement forces the endorser to risk part of their own locked stake.
